contract_plain_english: Finite volume methods divide the domain into grid cells and approximate the average of q in each cell, meaning its integral over that cell divided by the cell volume. At each time step these approximate values change through fluxes at cell edges. The primary design problem is to construct numerical flux functions from the available approximate cell averages that approximate the correct fluxes reasonably well [raw PDF p.27, printed p.5, §1.2, first paragraph]. This is a qualitative description founded on integral conservation; the selected passage supplies no particular discrete update formula or quantified accuracy guarantee [same paragraph: reference to (1.10), 'modified in each time step', and 'reasonably well'].
